correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every feasible labeling to two shore-sum inequalities. Because a matching deletion removes at most one neighbor per potential defender, the defender surcharge is at least \(\phi_p(z)=\min\{\lceil z/p\rceil,2\lceil(z-1)/p\rceil\}\). The elementary \(H_m\) bound gives the global lower bound, including the all-zero-shore boundary, and a two-defender construction attains it. Exhaustive definition-level checks for all matching sizes on \(G_{3,3,t}\) and \(G_{3,4,t}\) with \(p\in\{3,4,5\}\) agree exactly.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic searches found no \(p\)-strong Roman theorem for crowns or complete bipartite graphs with a matching deleted. The 2024 defining paper was inspected in full: Proposition 15 covers \(K_{r,s}\), its exact-value summary names complete bipartite graphs and bi-stars, and full-text searches found no crown or matching treatment. The closest stronger-looking 2026 paper treats ordinary strong Roman domination, corresponding to \(p=2\), including crowns, but not \(p\)-strong Roman domination for \(p\ge3\). The claimed matching-deletion formula is not an implication of either result because edge deletion has competing effects on adjacency to defenders and defender load.
residual_risks: An older or very recent p-strong Roman result could be poorly indexed or use alternate notation not recovered by the searches.
The 2026 ordinary strong-Roman crown result is close structurally; future literature could already have generalized it to p-strong domination without using crown/matching keywords.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete robustness theorem across every matching size, not a single graph value. It simultaneously extends the published undeleted-biclique \(p\)-strong formula to matching deletions and gives all crown graphs for every \(p\ge3\), complementing the recent ordinary strong-Roman crown result. The matching condition is natural and the proof isolates the exact structural reason: every defender loses at most one cross-neighbor.
